purpose: Comprehensive step library for the Line Dancing creator app. step_pattern/footwork_primitive carry counts, signed net_rotation_deg (+=CW/right), and foot continuity (foot_end = free foot after = what the next step starts on). styling/concept carry vocabulary only.
provenance: Common line-dance vocabulary assembled with teaching references as guides. The named moves are established vocabulary, not inventions attributed to a guide author or this app. All existing entries, aliases and mechanical fields are retained. Source-specific editorial notes and selected explanations were revised on 2026-09-03. Historical source records and the original reference files are preserved privately. This update is not an independent instructor review or a blanket claim of original authorship over the retained descriptions.

conventions.foot_continuity: next.foot_start must equal current free_foot (or either); then free_foot <- foot_end
conventions.parity: odd weight_changes switch the free foot, even keep it
conventions.ab_safe: true only for safest absolute-beginner staples; the AB generator honors this flag

steps.name: Balance
steps.description: General term for maintaining body equilibrium/control over the supporting foot.
steps.flags: Terminology only. May overlap with Balance Step; check whether the choreography means general balance or the counted movement.

steps.name: Ball
steps.description: The ball (front pad) of the foot; used to describe weight placement.
steps.flags: Foot-part terminology, distinct from the movement Ball Change.

steps.name: Beats
steps.description: A unit of measure of rhythmic time in the music.
steps.flags: Terminology.

steps.name: Bpm
steps.description: Beats per minute; a measure of a track's tempo, counted from the strongest beat.
steps.flags: Tempo terminology, not a counted movement.

steps.name: Break
steps.description: To reverse direction; the 6-count pattern in swing is called a break pattern.
steps.flags: Direction-change terminology. Break Step can also mean a rock step, so confirm the intended action in the choreography.

steps.name: Bridge
steps.description: A break from standard phrasing in the music, and the added sequence of steps inserted into the dance to compensate for it.
steps.flags: Choreography-structure terminology, related to tags and restarts; no fixed movement counts are specified.

steps.name: Cha Cha
steps.description: A dance rhythm counted 1&2, 3&4.
steps.flags: Stored as rhythm terminology, with count notation for reference. A danced triple-step interpretation uses 1&2; select an explicit movement definition when building a sequence.

steps.name: Clockwise
steps.description: Movement from left to right, the way a clock's hands move; the + (right) rotation direction.
steps.flags: Direction terminology, not a counted movement.

steps.name: Count
steps.description: Used to time weight changes: slow (2 beats), quick (1 beat), 'and' (half a quick count).
steps.flags: Timing terminology, not a movement with its own fixed footwork.

steps.name: Count "&"
steps.description: In a straight subdivision such as 1&2, the & labels the halfway point between the numbered counts. The chosen rhythm determines the subdivision.
steps.flags: Subdivision terminology, not a movement with its own fixed footwork.

steps.name: Counter Clockwise
steps.description: Movement from right to left, opposite clockwise; the - (left) rotation direction.
steps.flags: Direction terminology, not a counted movement.

steps.name: Diagonal
steps.description: A direction that is 45 degrees away from the center of the line of dance.
steps.flags: Direction terminology, not a standalone danced movement.

steps.name: Forward
steps.description: Travel toward the direction the dancer is facing.
steps.flags: Direction terminology, not a standalone danced movement.

steps.name: Home
steps.description: Return to the starting location.
steps.flags: Position or facing terminology, not a counted movement.

steps.name: Phrased
steps.description: A dance is 'phrased' when choreographed to fit the music exactly; tags, bridges, or structured parts keep it in phrase.
steps.flags: Choreography-structure terminology, not a standalone movement.

steps.name: Restart
steps.description: Restarting a dance from the beginning at a specified interval in the choreography.
steps.flags: Terminology, not a move.

steps.name: Rhythm
steps.description: The recurring flow of heavy and light accents in music; these accents drive the pattern of foot and body movements that becomes a dance.
steps.flags: Timing terminology; no fixed movement counts or footwork are specified.

steps.name: Spot Dance
steps.description: A dance executed in one area or spot (does not travel around the floor).
steps.flags: Dance-position terminology, not a fixed sequence of steps.

steps.name: Stationary Turn
steps.description: A rotation in place, taking one or more weight changes to complete.
steps.flags: A class of turns performed in place. Counts and rotation depend on the particular turn and are not specified by this terminology entry.

steps.name: Syncopation
steps.description: Use of the off-beats (the '&' counts in between whole beats), e.g. shuffle, kick-ball-change.
steps.flags: Timing terminology; the actual subdivision and movement must be specified in the choreography.

steps.name: Tag
steps.description: An addition to a dance sequence inserted at points in the music to keep the dance in phrase with the track.
steps.flags: Choreography-structure terminology. A particular tag needs its own counts and movements.

steps.name: Tempo
steps.description: The speed of a piece of music.
steps.flags: Timing terminology, not a counted movement.

steps.name: Turn
steps.description: A movement made to change direction.
steps.flags: General movement terminology. A particular turn needs its own duration, direction, rotation and footwork.

steps.name: Turn In
steps.description: A turn that rotates in the opposite direction of the weighted foot.
steps.flags: Turn-direction terminology, not a complete counted movement.

steps.name: Turn Out
steps.description: A turn that rotates in the same direction as the weighted foot.
steps.flags: Turn-direction terminology, not a complete counted movement.

steps.name: Waltz
steps.description: A rhythm with 3 beats to each bar of music; waltz-timed dances are organized in sections of three or six steps, usually a step per count.
steps.flags: Rhythm and timing terminology, not a complete movement sequence.

steps.name: Across
steps.description: Describes one foot moving in front of another (a cross in front).
steps.flags: Verified: R + 1 wc (odd) -> L. Directional descriptor synonymous with a cross-in-front. Weight-bearing when danced as a stepping cross (1 wc, canonical); a pure modifier is weightless (0 wc).

steps.name: Ball Change
steps.description: A quick change of weight from one foot (ball) to the other and back, usually preceded by a kick or heel touch.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R. Two quick weight changes spanning ~1 beat (syncopated '&1'); net weight returns to the standing foot. Commonly the tail of kick-ball-change / heel-ball-change.
steps.seed_note: Syncopated &2 — borrows the '&' of the previous beat and lands on the next downbeat, so it effectively consumes ~1 beat (I set counts=1; flag the syncopation, it is not a clean whole beat). Two quick opposite weight changes (even) -> free foot UNCHANGED. Building block of kick-ball-change and paddle turns. Mirrors.

steps.name: Behind
steps.description: Describes one foot crossing behind the other (a cross behind).
steps.flags: Verified: R + 1 wc (odd) -> L. Weight-bearing when danced as a stepping cross-behind (as in a grapevine), 1 wc. As a pure modifier it can be weightless. Travels sideways when used inside a vine.

steps.name: Brush
steps.description: Use the ball of the free foot to brush the floor as the foot swings forward or back.
steps.flags: Verified: 0 wc -> free foot unchanged. Directional variants (forward, back, across) and L/R collapsed. Close to scuff but not on the ab_safe staple list, so ab_safe false.

steps.name: Chug
steps.description: Keep support on the same foot as you make a short forward scooting action; the free foot remains lifted.
steps.flags: Stored model: no weight transfer; support stays on the scooting foot. A hip-hop turning variant uses the free foot to push while the weighted foot stays in place; that variant needs a nonzero rotation.

steps.name: Cross
steps.description: Cross one foot over the other, taking weight (e.g. cross R over L).
steps.flags: Verified: R + 1 wc (odd) -> L. Distinct from 'Behind' (cross behind) and 'Across' (front descriptor). Not on the ab_safe staple list.

steps.name: Cross Kick
steps.description: Kick the free foot across the standing leg (e.g. kick R across L).
steps.flags: Verified: 0 wc -> free foot unchanged. Kick=Beginner; kept ab_safe false as a cross variant. L/R collapsed.

steps.name: Diagonal Kick
steps.description: Kick the free foot diagonally forward toward the same side (e.g., right foot kicks diagonally forward-right).
steps.flags: Verified: 0 wc -> free foot unchanged. Not separately leveled; judged Beginner from Kick. ab_safe kept false as a directional variant.

steps.name: Dig
steps.description: Touch the ball or heel of the free foot to the floor with a strong emphasis.
steps.flags: Stored model: a weightless accent touch with no change of free foot. This entry is not included in the AB filter.

steps.name: Drag
steps.description: Draw the free foot toward the standing foot over the allotted counts. For this version, finish without transferring weight to the closing foot.
steps.flags: Stored model: no weight transfer and the free foot stays unchanged. A closing step can instead transfer weight once and switch the free foot. Duration may be one or two slow beats; confirm the ending and timing for the choreography.

steps.name: Fan
steps.description: Use the heel as a pivot and open the toes to the side, then bring them back. This toe-fan version is separate from a heel fan.
steps.flags: Stored model: no weight transfer and the free foot stays unchanged. This is the generic fan entry; Heel Fan and Toe Fan describe separate variants.

steps.name: Flare
steps.description: A low kick on or near the floor.
steps.flags: Stored model: no weight transfer and the free foot stays unchanged. The action may be a low sweeping or circular kick; confirm the intended variation.

steps.name: Flick
steps.description: The heel flicks back or out to the side.
steps.flags: Stored model: a heel-flick action with no weight transfer and no change of free foot. Do not treat this entry as an Applejack.

steps.name: Heel Bounce
steps.description: With weight on the balls of both feet, lift and drop the heels.
steps.flags: Stored model: both feet participate, weight stays on the balls of the feet, and no transfer is counted. A single free foot is not specified, so ordinary free-foot parity does not apply. May repeat rhythmically on & counts.

steps.name: Heel Clicks
steps.description: Rise onto the balls of the feet and click the heels together.
steps.flags: Stored model: both feet participate and no weight transfer is counted. A single free foot is not specified, so ordinary free-foot parity does not apply.

steps.name: Heel Fan
steps.description: With weight on the ball of the foot, twist (fan) the heel out to the side and return it to center.
steps.flags: Stored model: no weight transfer and the free foot stays unchanged. Distinct from the generic Fan and Toe Fan entries.

steps.name: Heel Twist
steps.description: With weight on the balls of the feet and feet together, move both heels to one side and then back to center.
steps.flags: Stored model: both feet participate with weight on the balls and no counted transfer. Ordinary free-foot parity does not apply. The heels may twist left or right.

steps.name: Hitch
steps.description: Lift the knee up (bent), foot off the floor.
steps.flags: Stored model: no weight transfer and the free foot stays unchanged. Included in the AB filter as a catalog setting.
steps.seed_note: 1-count weightless filler, raises the free knee. Often replaces the touch at the end of a vine. Weight-neutral -> does not affect continuity.

steps.name: Hold
steps.description: A pause with no movement (a held count).
steps.flags: Freeze is an alias. Stored model: no weight transfer and no change of free foot. A hold may last one or more beats; specify its duration. Included in the AB filter as a catalog setting.
steps.seed_note: 1-count pause consuming a beat with no weight change; whatever foot was free stays free. Useful for the assembler to pad phrasing to fill a musical count without altering continuity. Can span multiple counts if written 'hold 2'.

steps.name: Hook
steps.description: Lift the foot and cross it in front of the supporting leg (at the shin/ankle).
steps.flags: Stored model: no weight transfer and the free foot stays unchanged. This entry is not included in the AB filter.

steps.name: Hop
steps.description: A jump on the spot off one foot, landing on the same foot.
steps.flags: Stored model: landing on the same supporting foot, with no transfer between feet. This entry is not included in the AB filter.

steps.name: Jumping Jacks
steps.description: A jump landing with feet apart, then returning to centre; often syncopated and sometimes returning to a crossed position.
steps.flags: Both feet bear weight, so there is no single free foot and the number of weight transfers is unspecified. The stored pattern is symmetric and not mirrorable. Timing may be syncopated as 1&2.

steps.name: Kick
steps.description: A leg-lift from the knee in any direction; the knee does not fully straighten. Weightless - the working foot stays free.
steps.flags: Verified: 0 wc -> working foot stays free. Directional variants folded here; cross-kick and diagonal-kick are separate records. ab_safe staple.
steps.seed_note: 1-count weightless filler; the kicking foot is the currently free foot and stays free. Pairs into kick-ball-change or double kicks. Weight-neutral, so it never breaks foot continuity.

steps.name: Knee Pops
steps.description: Push the knee forward, lifting the heel off the floor while the ball of the foot stays in contact. Usually done as a repeated sequence.
steps.flags: Stored model: isolation without weight transfer. The one-count-per-pop duration is approximate; a sequence of pops may use different timing. This movement also has a styling interpretation.

steps.name: Leap
steps.description: Take off from one supporting foot and land with weight on the other. The receiving foot becomes the new support.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 1 wc (odd) -> L (lead switches). Canonical R-lead = land on R (take-off from L), so foot_end=L is the free foot. Take-off foot is opposite the landing foot.

steps.name: Louie Louis
steps.description: With one foot ahead of the other and weight on the balls of both feet, knees slightly bent, swivel both heels inward then back to centre.
steps.flags: Stored model: a symmetric heel swivel involving both feet, with no transfer between feet.

steps.name: Lunge
steps.description: Transfer weight onto a bent leg with the free leg extended.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 1 wc (odd) -> L (free foot becomes the extended leg). Usually to the side but can be forward; travels flagged.

steps.name: Mashed Potatoes
steps.description: A swivel novelty step: with weight on the balls of the feet, swivel heels out then in (knees rotate in/out), typically traveling.
steps.flags: Stored mechanics are provisional and need review. Counts are approximate, and classification as footwork or styling is uncertain.

steps.name: Pigeon Toed
steps.description: Traveling sideways: bring the toes together leaving heels apart, then bring the heels together leaving toes apart (weight alternating toe/heel).
steps.flags: Swivel travel (weight on toe/heel, no clean transfer -> 0 wc). Same movement as Traveling Applejacks (step_pattern) but kept separate as the primitive form.

steps.name: Point
steps.description: Point the toe to the side (or forward/back) with no weight.
steps.flags: Verified: 0 wc -> working foot stays free. ab_safe staple.

steps.name: Press
steps.description: Step forward (or back) onto the ball of the free foot with partial weight, supporting leg straight, pressed knee bent, body leaning slightly.
steps.flags: Partial weight; modeled as weightless press-and-recover (0 wc) -> becomes a full 1 wc/switch if the press is committed. Direction fwd or back.

steps.name: Recover
steps.description: Shift weight back onto the (previously free) foot, stepping in the original/in-place position; the recover half of a rock-recover.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 1 wc (odd) -> L. Not on the ab_safe staple list.

steps.name: Ronde de Jambe
steps.description: With weight on one foot, sweep the free (pointed-toe) foot around in an arc.
steps.flags: 0 wc (free foot sweeps) -> continuity-neutral. Can incorporate a turn (then non-zero rotation). counts approximate.

steps.name: Scoot
steps.description: A hop/slide forward on the supporting foot (a loop or jump with forward movement).
steps.flags: Stored model: support remains on the same foot, with no weight transfer or change of free foot.

steps.name: Scuff
steps.description: Brush the heel of the free foot forward along the floor; weight stays on the supporting foot.
steps.flags: 0 wc -> continuity-safe. ab_safe staple. Often ends a vine.
steps.seed_note: 1-count weightless filler (a heel brush; a 'brush' is the toe/ball version). Commonly ends a vine. Weight-neutral -> continuity-safe.

steps.name: Slap
steps.description: Use of the hand to slap the heel or knee.
steps.flags: Upper-body accent, no foot weight change -> continuity-neutral. Could also be styling.

steps.name: Slide
steps.description: Glide a foot across the floor in the specified direction. This entry models a slide that takes weight; a slide ending with an unweighted touch has a different exit foot.
steps.flags: Stored model: the weighted version transfers once, changing the free foot from R to L. A slide ending in a touch can instead have no transfer and leave the free foot unchanged. Confirm the version in the sheet.

steps.name: Splits
steps.description: Heel split: weight on balls of both feet, move both heels out then back together. Toe split: weight on both heels, move both toes out then back together.
steps.flags: MERGED: standalone 'Heel Split' (footwork_primitive, Beginner) folded in here (this record already collapses heel + toe splits). Both-feet symmetric; weight redistributes but no net change -> continuity-neutral. Not on ab_safe list.

steps.name: Stamp
steps.description: Strike the floor with the free foot for an accented sound. This entry uses the unweighted version: lift or release that foot without moving body weight onto it.
steps.flags: Stored model: the unweighted stomp-up interpretation, with no transfer and no change of free foot. A weighted stamp transfers once and switches the free foot. Confirm the intended interpretation. This entry is not included in the AB filter.

steps.name: Step
steps.description: The movement of a foot with a change of weight.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 1 wc (odd) -> L. The atomic weighted step. Bare 'step' not on the ab_safe staple list.

steps.name: Stomp
steps.description: Stomp the foot down beside the other. Plain 'stomp' takes weight; 'stomp up' is a weightless accent.
steps.flags: Stored model: a weighted R stomp transfers once and leaves L free. A stomp-up takes no weight and leaves the free foot unchanged. Included in the AB filter as a catalog setting.
steps.seed_note: FLAG the continuity fork: a plain 'STOMP' plants the foot and TAKES weight (free foot switches to the other foot), whereas 'STOMP UP' is a weightless accent (free foot unchanged). The assembler must read which the sheet means — this is the one filler that can change weight.

steps.name: Stride
steps.description: A large step forward or back.
steps.flags: Stored model: one weight transfer changes the free foot from R to L.

steps.name: Sweep
steps.description: Arc the pointed toe of the free foot out and around, from front to back or back to front.
steps.flags: Stored model: a free-foot arc with no weight transfer or change of free foot. A turning sweep needs a nonzero rotation. Related to Ronde; confirm the intended duration and turn.

steps.name: Swivel
steps.description: A movement of the heels or toes while weight is on the opposite part of the foot; e.g. weight on heels, swivel both toes to a side and return.
steps.flags: Stored model: weight redistributes without a net change of support. Often involves both feet; a single free-foot transition is not specified.

steps.name: Swivet
steps.description: Use a heel pivot under one foot and a toe pivot under the other to turn both feet together, then return. Reverse the heel-and-toe pairing for the opposite side.
steps.flags: Stored model: weight is on opposite parts of the feet with no net transfer between feet. The four-count Heel Swivets pattern is a separate variation.

steps.name: Toe Fan
steps.description: With weight on the other foot, fan the toe out to the side and return it to centre.
steps.flags: Stored model: a free-foot fan with no weight transfer or change of free foot. Distinct from the generic Fan and Heel Fan entries.

steps.name: Together
steps.description: Move the free foot next to the opposite (supporting) foot.
steps.flags: Weight fork: a weighted close ('step together') = 1 wc (R -> L, canonical here); a weightless close ('touch together') = 0 wc (free foot unchanged). The full 'step-together' 2-count move is the ab_safe staple; this bare primitive set ab_safe false.

steps.name: Touch
steps.description: Tap the toe or heel of the free foot without taking weight.
steps.flags: 0 wc -> continuity-safe. 'Tap' is a synonym. Distinct from 2-count 'step touch'. ab_safe staple.
steps.seed_note: 1-count weightless filler (distinct from 'step touch' which is 2 counts). The touching foot stays free. Weight-neutral -> continuity-safe. Mirrors.

steps.name: Walk
steps.description: Place the next foot in the chosen direction and transfer weight onto it. Alternate feet for a sequence of walks.
steps.flags: Stored model: one weighted step changes the free foot from R to L. Often used in a series. This entry is not included in the AB filter.

steps.name: Weight Change
steps.description: Shifting body weight from the supporting foot to the free foot.
steps.flags: Stored model: one transfer changes the free foot from R to L. Also used as terminology for the transfer itself.

steps.name: Ankle Rock
steps.description: With feet crossed and ankles locked, rock weight onto the forward foot, then return weight to the back foot.
steps.flags: Stored model: two weight transfers leave R free. Entry foot is ambiguous when starting with crossed ankles; the stored R entry is one interpretation and needs checking. The crossed-ankle position may be more demanding than a plain rock.

steps.name: Balance ½ Turn
steps.description: Step forward R, step forward L, pivot 1/2 turn right (canonical).
steps.flags: Verified: R + 3 wc (odd) -> L; +180 sane for a step-step-pivot. Pivot counted as 1 beat (could be read as 4 counts if step+pivot each get a beat). Net +180 for the R/clockwise version.

steps.name: Balance Step
steps.description: A step in any direction followed by a close step and then a step in place (or a hold); mostly used in waltzes. Collapses forward/back directional variants.
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers change the free foot from R to L. If the final count is a hold instead of a step in place, there are two transfers and R remains free. Directional versions share this entry; confirm the stated lead and ending for each use.

steps.name: Boogie Walk
steps.description: A forward-traveling styled walk (= camel walk): step forward, slide the other foot up beside, step forward again, with a circular hip transfer to the moving leg.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 3 wc (odd) -> L. Boogie Walk and Camel Walk are the same move (merged). Middle slide/drag weighting ambiguous - treated as a weight change to make the two forward steps work (3 wc); some notate it as 2 wc with a pure drag.

steps.name: Box Step
steps.description: Step, close, step (side or forward), touch - four counts tracing a box shape on the floor. Collapses forward/side and L/R variants.
steps.flags: Stored model: four counts with an unweighted touch on count 4, giving three transfers and leaving L free from an R start. Box Steps can also mean an eight-count sequence of two linked boxes; confirm the intended length.

steps.name: Break Turn
steps.description: Step forward and take weight on the forward foot, turn (1/8, 1/4, or 1/2) in the opposite direction of the forward foot, then take weight on the other foot. A step-turn / military-pivot family move.
steps.flags: Stored model: two transfers leave R free. Turn amount is unspecified and may be 1/8, 1/4 or 1/2; an R-forward version turns left, opposite the forward foot. Travel is variable, including in-place and backward interpretations. Military Turn, Military Pivot, Step Turn and Chase Turn can refer to this family; confirm the exact count, direction and travel rather than relying on a name alone.

steps.name: Charleston
steps.description: Kick forward, step forward beside the other foot, touch the opposite toe back, step back beside - 4 counts rocking forward and back.
steps.flags: Stored model: two transfers leave R free; the kick and touch take no weight. This entry is not included in the AB filter.
steps.seed_note: AB staple, danced roughly on the spot. Only 2 of the 4 counts take weight (the kick and back-touch are weightless) -> even changes, free foot UNCHANGED (R free start and end). Some sheets end count 4 with a weighted step back on R (then L free) — check the ending. Mirrors.

steps.name: Coaster Step
steps.description: Three weight-taking steps, usually syncopated (1&2): back, together, forward (or the forward version: forward, together, back).
steps.flags: Verified: R + 3 wc (odd) -> L; 3 wc compressed into 2 beats (1&2). Both forward and back variants exist; both net ~on_spot, collapsed. Can be slowed to full counts (~3 beats).
steps.seed_note: Counted 1&2 = 2 beats. Back-together-forward on the SAME lead foot (R steps back and forward). Three weight changes (odd) -> free foot SWITCHES: R-lead ends L free. A 'forward coaster' (forward-together-back) mirrors the shape but same count/continuity logic. Mirrors.

steps.name: Cross & Unwind
steps.description: Cross one foot over the other and unwind a 1/2 turn (canonical: cross R over L, unwind 1/2 turn left).
steps.flags: Stored model: two transfers leave R free, with an R cross followed by a half turn left (-180 degrees). The opposite version crosses L and turns right (+180 degrees). Some choreographies use a three-quarter unwind (+/-270 degrees); confirm the amount.

steps.name: Cross Rock
steps.description: Cross-rock one foot over (forward or back), then rock back onto the other foot.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R. Forward and back variants plus L/R collapsed. ab_safe false - crossing adds complexity over a plain rock.
steps.seed_note: A rock step where the working foot crosses OVER instead of stepping forward. Two opposite weight changes (even) -> free foot UNCHANGED (R crosses and R ends free). Distinct from the scissor step (no 'together' and no final weighted cross). Mirrors.

steps.name: Cross Shuffle
steps.description: A syncopated crossing triple: cross over, small step to the side, cross over again (1&2).
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers across two beats change the free foot from R to L. Uses a cross-side-cross interpretation. Confirm that the chosen lead and written crossing directions agree before use.

steps.name: Electric Kicks
steps.description: Hip-hop move: step forward on R while kicking L low behind; step back on L while kicking R low forward; step back on R while kicking L low forward; step forward on L while kicking R low behind.
steps.flags: Stored model: four weighted steps, each paired with a simultaneous low kick, leave R free. Hip-hop-style pattern with approximately in-place travel; review its coordination and space needs.

steps.name: Extended Grapevine
steps.description: The basic grapevine continued in the same side-traveling pattern for additional steps.
steps.flags: Variable length ('basic grapevine continued') -> typically 5-8 weighted steps; counts, weight_changes and foot_end depend on the chosen length. Left flagged. Judged Beginner (grapevine family).

steps.name: Grapevine
steps.description: A three-step traveling side move - step to the side, cross the other foot behind, step to the side - that often ends on count 4 with a touch, step or kick.
steps.flags: Stored model: a touch on count 4 gives three transfers and leaves L free from an R start. A weighted step on count 4 instead gives four transfers and leaves R free. Included in the AB filter as a catalog setting.
steps.seed_note: Safest AB staple. Travels sideways in lead-foot direction. CONTINUITY CRUX: the 4th count decides the free foot. If it is a TOUCH/scuff/hitch/kick of L (as notated), weight stays on R and L is free -> the free foot SWITCHES (R-lead ends L free). If the 4th count is a weighted STEP L (common 'vine, step' ending), weight goes to L and R stays free -> free foot UNCHANGED. Assembler must know which ending a given sheet uses. Mirrors to L-lead.

steps.name: Grapevine 1/4 Turn
steps.description: A grapevine whose final step makes a 1/4 turn (canonical: step right to side, cross left behind right, step right making a 1/4 turn right).
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers leave L free from an R start. The turn is a quarter right (+90 degrees); the opposite version turns left (-90 degrees). This is the quarter-turn variation, not a half turn. This turning entry is not included in the AB filter.

steps.name: Heel Ball Change
steps.description: Touch the heel forward, then a ball-change: step onto that foot beside the other, then step the other foot in place.
steps.flags: Stored model: two transfers leave R free; the heel touch takes no weight. Timing is 1&2.

steps.name: Heel Ball Cross
steps.description: Touch the heel forward, step that foot slightly back, then cross the other foot over it.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R (heel touch weightless). Syncopated 1&2. Not separately leveled; judged Intermediate (kick/heel-ball-cross family).
steps.seed_note: FLAG: this family is the least standardized. Counted syncopated (&1&2 or 1&2&) = ~2 beats. Two common resolutions: (a) HEEL JACK ending in a TOUCH/close (weight stays on the standing foot, e.g. glossary version 'step back, touch heel forward, step down, touch together' -> free foot switches, ends with the heel foot free); (b) HEEL BALL CROSS ending in a weighted CROSS (as notated, ending weight on the crossing R, L free). The syncopation and the ending both vary by sheet — the assembler should treat count as ~2 and confirm the ending weight from the specific choreography rather than trusting a default.

steps.name: Heel Grind
steps.description: Rock forward onto the heel, arcing the toe across over two counts, then return the weight back onto the other foot.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R. Weight-bearing grind (forward onto heel then recover). Styling overlaps with Grind (Improver); classified step_pattern for its clear 2-count weighted mechanics.

steps.name: Heel Jack
steps.description: Step diagonally back on one foot, touch the opposite heel diagonally forward, step that foot back to center, then touch/step the first foot beside it.
steps.flags: Verified for the touch reading: R + 2 wc (even) -> R. COUNT-4 FORK: as a STEP weight_changes=3 and foot_end=L (odd). Related to Vaudeville/Heel Jacks (Intermediate). Often syncopated (1&2&). Net travel ~on-spot.

steps.name: Heel Pivot
steps.description: Step side or back, turning in the opposite direction of the weighted foot; bring the feet together and turn on both heels; then step forward on the un-weighted foot.
steps.flags: Turn amount is unspecified; a half turn is one possible version. Stored model: two transfers, with either-foot entry/exit fields rather than a fixed free-foot pair. Confirm the turn and support sequence; ordinary fixed-foot parity does not resolve them.

steps.name: Heel Strut
steps.description: Step forward onto the heel (count 1), then drop the toe taking weight (count 2).
steps.flags: Stored model: two counts but only one transfer, changing the free foot from R to L. Heel placement and the following toe drop form that single transfer. Travels forward. Included in the AB filter as a catalog setting.
steps.seed_note: AB staple. Two counts but ONE weight change (weight lands on R when toe drops) -> free foot SWITCHES (R-lead ends L free). Usually travels forward. Mirrors.

steps.name: Heel Swivets
steps.description: A 4-count swivet: fan one toe out and the opposite heel out; return the feet and shift weight to the other heel/toe; fan the other toe and opposite heel out; return the feet.
steps.flags: Weight redistributes between heels and toes, so the number of whole-foot transfers is unspecified. The stored pattern already covers both sides and is not mirrorable. Distinct from the two-count Swivet primitive; review support changes for the chosen execution.

steps.name: Heel Turn
steps.description: Same as a heel pivot except it ends by stepping forward on the opposite foot.
steps.flags: Turn amount is unspecified; a half turn is one possible version. Stored model: two transfers, with either-foot entry/exit fields rather than a fixed free-foot pair. Confirm the turn and support sequence; ordinary fixed-foot parity does not resolve them.

steps.name: Jazz Box
steps.description: Cross R over L, step back on L, step R to R side, close L beside R. A four-count box danced in place.
steps.flags: Stored model: four transfers leave R free. The entry is included in the AB filter despite its Improver level label; those are separate catalog settings, not a certification of difficulty or safety.
steps.seed_note: AB staple. 4 weight changes (even) so the free foot is UNCHANGED: R-lead starts R free and ends R free. Very portable in the assembler. Variant seen on some sheets starts with a forward step then crosses; ending free foot is the same. Mirrors to L-lead.

steps.name: Jazz Box 1/4 Turn
steps.description: Cross R over L, step back on L, step R making 1/4 turn right, close L beside R.
steps.flags: Stored model: four transfers leave R free. The R-leading version turns a quarter right (+90 degrees); its opposite turns left.

steps.name: Kick Ball Change
steps.description: Kick R forward, step onto ball of R beside L, change weight onto L in place. Ends on the same lead (R free).
steps.flags: Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R (kick weightless; the ball-change returns the free foot). Kick-ball-changes keep you on the same lead.
steps.seed_note: Counted 1&2 (syncopated) = 2 beats. Net effect is an in-place weight keeper: R kicks, and R ends free again (even net weight change). Very common; taught early but the & syncopation nudges it above pure AB. Mirrors.

steps.name: Kick Ball Cross
steps.description: Kick R forward, step onto ball of R, cross L over R. Ends with R free.
steps.flags: Stored model: two transfers leave R free; the kick takes no weight. Uses a kick-ball-cross interpretation. Confirm that the kicking foot, ball step and final crossing foot agree in the chosen variant.

steps.name: Lock Step
steps.description: Step forward R, lock L behind R, step forward R (forward version). A syncopated triple with a locked middle step; also danced backward (lock crosses in front).
steps.flags: Verified: R + 3 wc (odd) -> L. Timing varies: 1&2 (shuffle-timed), 1,2& (Wizard note), or 3 full counts. Forward & back variants folded (travels=varies).
steps.seed_note: A shuffle whose middle step LOCKS tightly behind (forward travel) or in front (backward travel) instead of closing. Counted 1&2 = 2 beats, three weight changes (odd) -> free foot SWITCHES (R-lead forward lockstep ends L free). FLAG: a simpler 2-count 'step-lock' (step R, lock L) with even count 1,2 also exists and ends with weight on the LOCK foot (L) — different ending; check whether the sheet means the shuffle (1&2) or the plain step-lock. Mirrors.

steps.name: Mambo Step
steps.description: Rock forward R, recover onto L, step R beside L (forward mambo). Ends on the opposite lead; also danced back or to the side.
steps.flags: Stored model: the forward-mambo interpretation, with three transfers changing the free foot from R to L. Confirm the direction and foot sequence for the choreography before relying on these stored values.
steps.seed_note: Counted 1&2 = 2 beats: rock, recover, step. Three weight changes (odd) -> free foot SWITCHES (R-lead forward mambo ends weight on R, L free). Can be forward, back, or side mambo (rotation stays 0). A 'mambo 1/4 turn' adds ±90 on the 3rd step. FLAG: the 3rd step is variously written 'in place', 'together', or 'back' — all keep weight on R and L free. Mirrors.

steps.name: Monterey 1/2 Turn
steps.description: Touch R to R side; on the ball of L make a 1/2 turn right, stepping R beside L; touch L to L side; step L beside R.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R (the two touches are weightless); +180 sane for R-lead canonical (turns right); mirror turns left.

steps.name: Monterey 1/4 Turn
steps.description: Touch R to R side; on the ball of L make a 1/4 turn right, stepping R beside L; touch L to L side; step L beside R.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R (two touches weightless); +90 for R-lead (turns right); mirror opposite. Split from Monterey 1/2 per turn-amount rule.

steps.name: Paddle Turn
steps.description: A stationary turn rotating around one predominantly weighted, centralized foot while the other foot pushes off (paddles) around it.
steps.flags: Generic turning technique - total counts and net rotation vary with execution (commonly 1/4 per paddle unit); weight stays on the pivot foot (~0 net wc). Left flagged.
steps.seed_note: A series of small ball-change/push turns with weight staying over the PIVOT (support) foot. One 'paddle' = 2 counts = 1/4 turn (shown as -90, i.e. turning LEFT while the R foot pushes). FLAG: both count and direction vary widely — a 4-count paddle can make 1/2 turn (±180), and paddles are done to either side. The pushing foot (R) stays free throughout. Confirm per-sheet.

steps.name: Pivot 1/4 Turn
steps.description: Step forward R and pivot a 1/4 turn on the balls of both feet, changing weight.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R; R-lead rotates left (-90); mirror +90. Level inherited from Pivot Turn (Beginner).

steps.name: Pivot 3/4 Turn
steps.description: Step forward R and pivot a 3/4 turn on the balls of both feet, changing weight.
steps.flags: Stored model: two transfers leave R free. An R-leading version turns three quarters left (-270 degrees); its opposite turns right (+270 degrees). This larger turn may be more demanding than a half pivot.

steps.name: Pivot Turn
steps.description: One foot forward of the other; step forward R and pivot a 1/2 turn on the balls of both feet, changing weight. Feet stay on the floor.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R; R-lead canonical rotates LEFT (-180, CCW); mirror is +180. Default 1/2 pivot; 1/4 and 3/4 are separate records. Alias 'Step Turn' REMOVED (assigned to the Break Turn family to keep aliases unique). Not on the ab_safe staple list.

steps.name: Progressive Turn
steps.description: A traveling rotation of the body moving forward or backward down the line of dance.
steps.flags: Generic traveling turn - counts, rotation, and ending foot depend on execution (often a full turn over several steps). Left flagged.

steps.name: Push Step
steps.description: Use a step followed by a ball change, traveling in the direction given by the choreography. Confirm the rhythm and weight sequence for the intended version.
steps.flags: Stored model: the step-ball-change interpretation uses three transfers and leaves L free from an R start. Count and weight interpretation are uncertain; a one-beat ball-change reading can instead use two transfers. Confirm the intended version.

steps.name: Ramble
steps.description: To travel right or left by twisting the heels and toes along the floor.
steps.flags: Traveling heel-toe twist with unspecified counts and weight-transfer mechanics. These values need review before mechanical validation.

steps.name: Reverse Pivot
steps.description: Same movement as a basic pivot but the initial step is taken back instead of forward, then pivot.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R. Default 1/2 turn assumed (+180 canonical right); amount and direction vary by sheet. Level judged (pivot family is Beginner; reverse variant nudged to Improver).

steps.name: Rock Step
steps.description: Step onto a foot (forward, back, or side) taking weight, then recover weight back onto the other foot. Two opposite weight changes.
steps.flags: MERGED: standalone 'Back Rock' (rock-back variant, Beginner, ab_safe) folded in as aliases Back Rock/Rock Back. Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R. Collapses rock back/forward/left/right (direction does not change counts/rotation). 'Break step' alias REMOVED here (assigned to the Break concept to keep aliases unique). ab_safe staple.
steps.seed_note: AB staple. Two opposite weight changes on 2 beats. Can rock forward, back, or to the side (rock forward R/recover L shown; 'rock back R, recover L' is identical count/continuity). Even changes -> free foot UNCHANGED (R free start and end). Mirrors.

steps.name: Rock Step with 1/4 turn
steps.description: Rock to the side onto one foot, then recover onto the other while making a 1/4 turn.
steps.flags: Stored model: two transfers leave R free, with a quarter-right turn (+90 degrees) on the recovery; the opposite version turns left (-90 degrees). Other direction wording can describe a different variant, so confirm the chosen lead and turn.

steps.name: Rocking Chair
steps.description: Rock forward on one foot, recover, rock back on the same foot, recover; a rock-recover forward and back on the spot.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 4 wc (even) -> R. Distinct from 2-count rock step. ab_safe staple.
steps.seed_note: AB staple, danced on the spot. The SAME foot (R) does both rocks; even weight changes so free foot UNCHANGED (starts and ends R free). Do not confuse with 'rock step' (2 counts) — the rocking chair is a rock-recover forward AND back = 4 counts.

steps.name: Rolling Full Turn
steps.description: A full 360-degree turn traveling sideways over three steps: 1/4 turn, 1/2 turn, 1/4 turn (a rolling/unwinding vine).
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers change the free foot from R to L over a full right turn (+360 degrees); the opposite version turns left (-360 degrees). Distinct from Three Step Turn in how the rotation is distributed.
mechanics_review_notes: Shared rolling-vine aliases do not make the recorded full-turn and half-turn entries mechanically equivalent.

steps.name: Running Man
steps.description: Step forward on one foot while hitching the other knee and scooting the support foot back; alternate. A hip-hop illusion of running in place.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 2 wc (even) -> R (steps take weight, hitches weightless). Novelty/hip-hop; level judged. Appears to travel but scoots back on the spot.

steps.name: Sailor Step
steps.description: Cross one foot behind the other, step the other to the side, step first foot to place; a syncopated triple beginning with a cross behind.
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers change the free foot from R to L. Timing 1&2 occupies two beats.
steps.seed_note: Counted 1&2 = 2 beats, a shuffle-type step that begins with a cross BEHIND. Three weight changes (odd) -> free foot SWITCHES: R sailor (crossing R behind) ends weight on R, L free. A 'sailor 1/4 turn' variant adds ±90 but the plain sailor is 0. Mirrors.

steps.name: Sailor Step Turning
steps.description: A sailor step executed with a turn.
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers leave L free from an R start, with a quarter-right turn (+90 degrees). Quarter- and half-turn versions exist in either direction; confirm the amount and direction before use.

steps.name: Scissors
steps.description: Step to the side, close the other foot beside it, then cross the first foot over; a side-together-cross.
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers across 1&2 leave L free from an R start. Other versions use three or four straight counts, sometimes ending in a hold. Confirm the timing and ending rather than treating those versions as identical.
mechanics_review_notes: Scissors/Scissor Step names and aliases are retained. Confirm the specific side-close-cross timing and ending before equating this reference with any executable core scissors variation.

steps.name: Shuffle
steps.description: A syncopated three-step: step, close (feet do not pass), step. Traveling = shuffle (forward/back); side = chasse; in place = triple step.
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers across 1&2 leave L free from an R start. This entry covers forward/backward shuffles, side chasses and in-place triples. Direction changes do not by themselves alter its two-count duration or net rotation, but the travel direction must match the chosen version.
steps.seed_note: Counted 1&2 = 2 beats, THREE weight changes (odd) so the free foot SWITCHES: R-lead shuffle ends with L free. Can go forward, back, or to the side (side = 'chasse'). Direction of travel does not change rotation (0). This odd-switch is a key continuity rule for the assembler. Mirrors.

steps.name: Skate
steps.description: Move forward sliding one foot diagonally forward and taking weight, then slide the other foot diagonally forward in the opposite direction.
steps.flags: Stored model: two weighted glides leave R free.

steps.name: Spin
steps.description: Rotate around the supporting leg while the other leg stays free. The choreography specifies the direction, amount of turn and timing; the stored example is one full turn in one count.
steps.flags: Stored model: a full turn (+360 degrees) on the supporting foot, without a transfer during the spin. Other versions can turn three quarters (270 degrees) or in the opposite direction. Preparation and exit steps must be specified separately. Either-foot fields do not identify a fixed free-foot transition.

steps.name: Step Touch
steps.description: Step onto one foot, touch the other foot beside it (no weight).
steps.flags: Verified: R + 1 wc (odd) -> L (touch weightless). Can go side/forward/back. ab_safe staple.
steps.seed_note: The safest AB building block. One weight change (the touch takes no weight) -> free foot SWITCHES (R-lead ends L free / touching). Can go side, forward, or back. Mirrors.

steps.name: Stroll
steps.description: Two walking steps forward (step forward, step forward).
steps.flags: Stored model: two weight transfers leave R free.

steps.name: Strut
steps.description: Toe strut: place the toe (count 1), drop the heel with a weight change (count 2). Heel strut: place the heel (1), drop the ball with a weight change (2). Travels forward or back.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 1 wc (odd) -> L; two counts but ONE weight change. Collapses toe strut + heel strut (forward/back). ab_safe staple. NOTE the dedicated 'Heel Strut' record (forward-only, Beginner) is kept separately for its specific direction.

steps.name: Sugarfoot
steps.description: Touch the toe to the opposite instep, then touch the heel to the opposite instep (a novelty toe-in/heel-in pair); the swivel variant adds a heel swivel.
steps.flags: Stored model: both touches take no weight, leaving the free foot unchanged. Either-foot fields do not identify a fixed lead. Covers Sugarfoot and Sugarfoot Swivel styling variations; confirm the intended action.

steps.name: Switches
steps.description: Touch heel (or toe) forward, step it back beside the other, touch the other heel (or toe) forward, step it beside; alternating heel/toe switches.
steps.flags: Stored model: four counts with two weighted closing steps; touches are unweighted, leaving R free from an R start. A syncopated version uses 1&2& over two beats. Covers heel, toe and side switches; confirm duration and touch direction before use.

steps.name: Syncopated Grapevine
steps.description: The same footwork as a basic grapevine but timed with whole and half counts (1&2&), making it quicker.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 4 wc (even) -> R; 4 weighted steps compressed to 2 beats. Level judged (syncopation raises above plain Beginner vine).

steps.name: Three Step Turn
steps.description: A full rotation over three steps: step making 1/2 turn, step making 1/2 turn, then step forward on the free foot.
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers leave L free from an R start. Two half turns followed by a forward step make a full right turn (+360 degrees); the opposite version turns left (-360 degrees).

steps.name: Toe Heel Cross Swivels
steps.description: Isolate the upper body and swivel/pivot on the support foot while the free foot touches toe (to instep), then heel (forward), then crosses/locks over and takes weight; ends both feet facing the same direction.
steps.flags: Stored model: support stays on the same foot through the unweighted swiveling touches; only the final cross transfers weight, leaving L free from an R-working start. Foot mechanics are approximate and need review for the chosen version.

steps.name: Traveling Applejacks
steps.description: A pattern traveling sideways: bring toes together leaving heels apart, then heels together leaving toes apart, with weight on one toe and the opposite heel, then reversed, producing sideways travel.
steps.flags: Stored model: an approximate four-count, two-transfer interpretation leaves R free. Travel comes from heel/toe weight shifts. Counts and transfer mechanics need review. Related to the Pigeon Toed primitive.

steps.name: Triple Step Turn 1/4
steps.description: A triple step (1&2) executed while making a 1/4 turn.
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers leave L free from an R start, with a quarter-right turn (+90 degrees). The opposite version turns left (-90 degrees).

steps.name: Triple Step Turn 1/2
steps.description: A triple step / shuffle (1&2) executed while making a 1/2 turn.
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers leave L free from an R start, with a half-right turn (+180 degrees). The opposite version turns left (-180 degrees). Also called a shuffle half turn.

steps.name: Triple Step Turn 3/4
steps.description: A triple step (1&2) executed while making a 3/4 turn.
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers leave L free from an R start, with a three-quarter-right turn (+270 degrees). The opposite version turns left (-270 degrees).

steps.name: Triple Step Full Turn
steps.description: A triple step (1&2) executed while making a full turn.
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers leave L free from an R start, with a full-right turn (+360 degrees). The opposite version turns left (-360 degrees).

steps.name: Vaudeville
steps.description: Step diagonally back, cross the other foot over, step diagonally back again, then touch the crossing foot's heel to the forward diagonal; a crossing heel jack.
steps.flags: Stored model: three weighted steps and an unweighted heel touch leave L free from an R start. Syncopated timing is approximately 1&2& over two beats; some sheets use four counts. Distinct from Heel Jack because the footwork differs; confirm the notation and sequence.
steps.seed_note: Syncopated 1&2& = 2 beats (a cross, a side, a heel dig, a close). Related to the heel jack ('crossing heel jack'). Three weighted changes (cross R, side L, close R; the heel dig is weightless) -> free foot SWITCHES (R-lead ends L free). FLAG: often written as a repeating pair, so some sheets label the full unit '4 counts'; count and exact footwork vary — confirm per sheet. Mirrors.

steps.name: Weave
steps.description: Cross over, step to side, cross behind, step to side; like a vine but the crossing foot goes both in front and behind.
steps.flags: Verified: R + 4 wc (even) -> R. Travels sideways. ab_safe staple. Longer 6-8 count weaves exist; this is the 4-count unit.
steps.seed_note: Like a vine but the crossing foot goes both in FRONT and BEHIND (a vine only crosses behind). Travels sideways (this notation travels LEFT while R crosses). 4 weight changes (even) -> crossing foot R starts free and ends free (R free). Longer weaves (6-8 counts) exist; this is the common 4-count unit. Mirrors.

steps.name: Willies
steps.description: Travel forward using a pigeon-toe action, working through the balls of the feet. The exact rhythm and weight sequence need to be specified for the chosen variation.
steps.flags: Stored model: an estimated two-count, two-transfer interpretation leaves R free. Counts and weight-transfer mechanics remain uncertain and need review. Related to pigeon-toe movements.

steps.name: Wizard
steps.description: Step forward, lock the other foot behind, step forward again; a syncopated forward-traveling lockstep.
steps.flags: Stored model: three transfers leave L free from an R start. This syncopated lockstep uses 1,2& across two beats; preserve the late & timing rather than substituting 1&2.
mechanics_review_notes: Wizard/Dorothy uses the selected 1, 2& rhythm; the old 1&2 notation was corrected without changing duration, feet, or weight changes.

steps.name: Apple Jack
steps.description: Syncopated heel/toe swivel novelty, usually performed as a left+right pair: weight onto one heel and the opposite toe while swiveling the free toe/heel out to the side, then return feet to center.
steps.flags: MERGED: standalone styling entry 'Fancy Feet' (defined only as 'See apple jack') folded in as an alias. Classified styling/novelty per the project's authoritative reference doc. Does carry real syncopation (&1&2) and heel/toe weight placement, so it is borderline step_pattern. L+R collapsed. 'Traveling Applejacks' is a separate step_pattern entry.

steps.name: Body Alignment
steps.description: The body's three parts (upper torso, center, lower torso) held in stacked posture for proper alignment.
steps.flags: Technique/posture, no count or foot mechanics.

steps.name: Body Angle
steps.description: Angling the body away from the facing wall to prepare for the next step even while nominally facing that wall.
steps.flags: Body-orientation technique with overlapping styling and terminology uses; not a complete counted movement.

steps.name: Body Roll
steps.description: A ripple of the body up or down (forward, backward, or sideways) over a specified number of counts.
steps.flags: Styling performed over chosen counts, but this entry specifies no fixed duration or discrete foot/weight sequence. Count remains unspecified.

steps.name: Boogie
steps.description: The free hip lifts and moves in a circular motion away from the weighted foot.
steps.flags: Hip styling; no fixed movement sequence is specified here.

steps.name: Boogie Roll
steps.description: Add a rolling hip action to forward movement through a flexed knee, allowing the hip to trail the step. Treat this as styling applied to an explicitly counted foot pattern.
steps.flags: Hip styling; no fixed movement sequence is specified here.

steps.name: Center
steps.description: The body's balance point near the diaphragm; three centers are high (speed), medium (movement), and low (balance).
steps.flags: Body-technique term; listed among styling in the spec.

steps.name: Cuban Motion
steps.description: The contra movement of the hips during a cha cha; the hips move in opposite directions.
steps.flags: Hip technique treated as styling; not a complete counted footwork sequence.

steps.name: Frame
steps.description: Maintain a comfortable, organized posture through the torso and arms so balance and turns remain controlled. This is a body-positioning cue, not a counted step pattern.
steps.flags: Body-position and posture technique without a fixed count or discrete foot sequence.

steps.name: Grind
steps.description: Dig the heel of the foot into the floor with emphasis while the toes twist in and out, with some weight on the heel.
steps.flags: Foot/body styling. Use the Heel Grind movement entry when a counted, weight-bearing version is intended.

steps.name: Hip Bump
steps.description: Isolate and push the hip to one side (flexing the knees), bumping the hip in a given direction.
steps.flags: Bump is an alias for the hip-isolation action. A weighted four-count step-and-bump combination, such as a step with L-R-L hip bumps, needs its own weight-bearing mechanics rather than the uncounted styling entry.

steps.name: Hip Lift
steps.description: The hip lifts by straightening the non-supporting leg and leaving the heel up.
steps.flags: Hip-isolation styling, not a complete counted footwork sequence.

steps.name: Hip Roll
steps.description: Move the hips in a circular action, either clockwise or anti-clockwise.
steps.flags: Styling. Mirrorable (cw/ccw). Level judged Intermediate (Roll family).

steps.name: Posture
steps.description: Standing tall with all body parts stacked under the head. Smooth: hips tucked in one line; Rhythm: hips released into two units.
steps.flags: Body-technique/posture term; no count or foot mechanics.

steps.name: Roll
steps.description: The indicated body part circles right or left.
steps.flags: Styling; no discrete count/foot mechanics. Generic roll (see also Hip Roll / Body Roll).

steps.name: Shimmy
steps.description: Rapid alternating shoulder movement: as one shoulder moves forward the other moves back.
steps.flags: Styling; no discrete count/foot mechanics.

steps.name: Sway
steps.description: Rhythmically moving the upper torso to one side and/or the other.
steps.flags: Styling; no discrete count/foot mechanics.

steps.name: Torque
steps.description: A rotation of the upper body that twists and stretches the abdominal muscles, creating tension/energy to power a turn.
steps.flags: Styling without a specified duration or discrete footwork sequence.

steps.name: Vine with 1/4 turn
steps.description: step R, cross L behind R, step R turning 1/4 right, scuff/step L forward
steps.flags: Stored model: four counts, a quarter-right turn (+90 degrees), and an R-to-L free-foot transition. The number of weight transfers is unspecified; confirm the ending for the chosen variant.
steps.seed_note: The 1/4 turn is taken on count 3 so the dancer ends facing a new wall, then the 4th count steps/scuffs forward in the new direction. Value +90 = 1/4 turn RIGHT (clockwise); a 1/4-turn-LEFT vine = -90. Direction is choreographer's choice — I set +90 as the described version; flag that left is equally common. Same touch-vs-step continuity caveat as the plain vine.

steps.name: Vine with 1/2 turn
steps.description: step R turning 1/4 R, step L turning 1/2 R, step R turning 1/4 R, touch/step L
steps.flags: Stored model: four counts, a half-right turn (+180 degrees), and an R-to-L free-foot transition. The number of weight transfers is unspecified; confirm the turn distribution and ending for the chosen variant.
steps.seed_note: Often executed as a 'rolling vine' (full unwind: 1/4 + 1/2 + 1/4 across counts 1-3, ending the 1/2 turn, 4th count touches or steps). +180 = turn RIGHT; left version = -180. Higher difficulty than a static vine. Flag: some sheets label a '1/2 turn vine' that only rotates 180 total via a different distribution — net is still ±180.
mechanics_review_notes: Shared rolling-vine aliases do not make the recorded full-turn and half-turn entries mechanically equivalent.

steps.name: Jazz Box with 1/4 turn
steps.description: cross R over L, step back L turning 1/4 right, step R to side, step L forward
steps.flags: Stored model: four counts, a quarter-right turn (+90 degrees), and R free at both boundaries. The number of weight transfers is unspecified.
steps.seed_note: The 1/4 turn is taken on the 'step back L' (count 2). +90 = 1/4 turn RIGHT is the standard/most common jazz-box turn; a left version = -90 exists but is rarer. Still 4 weight changes so free foot is UNCHANGED (R free at end). Mirrors.

steps.name: Toe Strut
steps.description: touch R toe forward (1), drop R heel down taking weight (2)
steps.flags: Stored model: two counts, no net turn, and an R-to-L free-foot transition. The number of weight transfers is unspecified in this record.
steps.seed_note: AB staple. Same count/continuity as heel strut (one weight change, free foot switches to L). Toe-first instead of heel-first. Mirrors.

steps.name: Point / Touch
steps.description: point R toe to side (or touch beside), weight stays on L
steps.flags: Stored model: one count, no net turn, and R free at both boundaries. The number of weight transfers is unspecified; confirm whether the intended action takes weight.
steps.seed_note: 1 count, NO weight change -> the pointing/touching foot stays free (R free before and after). Often paired (point side, point together = 2 counts) or point-and-return (2 counts) — as a single gesture it is 1 count. Weight-neutral filler; extremely flexible for the assembler. Mirrors.

steps.name: Pivot Turn 1/2
steps.description: step R forward (1), pivot 1/2 turn left on balls of both feet, weight ends on L (2)
steps.flags: Stored model: two counts, a half-left turn (-180 degrees), and R free at both boundaries. The number of weight transfers is unspecified.
steps.seed_note: Default pivot = 1/2 turn (per glossaries). Step FORWARD on R, turn toward the back foot = LEFT/counterclockwise, so R-lead = -180. Two weight changes (even) -> free foot UNCHANGED (R free at end). Direction is dictated by lead foot: an L-lead forward step pivots RIGHT = +180. Sign here is for the R-lead version.

steps.name: Pivot Turn 1/4
